content.user_title: Generate Unit Tests for Existing Code
content.value_statement: Teams lose time writing repeatable unit tests and finding coverage gaps. This skill creates targeted test suites, mocks, and coverage guidance for common frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Python files for functions, classes, arguments, decorators, and docstrings.
Drafts pytest suites with success, empty input, and exception scenarios.
Drafts Jest tests for JavaScript and TypeScript functions.
Creates React component test outlines using Testing Library patterns.
Identifies coverage gaps from coverage report data.
Generates mock fixture patterns for external dependencies.
limitations: It focuses on unit tests, not full integration or end-to-end test suites.
It needs access to the source code under test.
Generated tests require review before use in production repositories.
Coverage commands may need project-specific configuration and user approval.

use_cases.title: Add Tests to Existing Modules
use_cases.description: Generate starter pytest or Jest coverage for functions and classes that currently lack unit tests.

use_cases.title: Improve Pull Request Confidence
use_cases.description: Create focused tests for changed code paths, edge cases, and expected failure behavior before review.

use_cases.title: Plan Coverage Improvements
use_cases.description: Use coverage output to identify weak areas and draft targeted tests for missing branches or functions.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Unit Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate unit tests for this file. Use the project test framework and include clear assertions for normal and invalid inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Edge Case Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for better behavior coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module and generate tests for boundary values, empty inputs, error paths, and important branches.

prompt_templates.title: Mock External Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for isolated unit tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate isolated unit tests for this code. Mock network, database, file system, and service dependencies where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Target Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this coverage report and source file to propose targeted unit tests for uncovered lines and branches.

output_examples.input: A Python utility module with public functions and no tests.
output_examples.output: A pytest suite outline with success cases, invalid input checks, exception tests, and fixture suggestions.

output_examples.input: A React component with props, state changes, and user interaction.
output_examples.output: A Testing Library plan covering rendering, visible state, event handling, and prop updates.

output_examples.input: A coverage report showing missed lines in a service module.
output_examples.output: A prioritized list of missing scenarios with suggested unit tests for each coverage gap.

best_practices: Provide the source file, current test framework, and expected behavior before asking for tests.
Review generated assertions against real business rules before committing tests.
Run generated tests in a trusted workspace after confirming any test command.
anti_patterns: Do not use generated tests as a substitute for understanding expected behavior.
Do not run coverage or test commands that you have not reviewed.
Do not request integration or browser tests when the task requires unit-only coverage.

faq.question: Which test frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It includes examples for pytest, Jest, JUnit, Go testing, and React Testing Library patterns.

faq.question: Can it write tests for private code?
faq.answer: Yes, if the source code is available in the current workspace or provided in the prompt.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: The skill can discuss coverage commands, but users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Will generated tests always pass?
faq.answer: No. Generated tests may need edits to match project setup, imports, fixtures, and exact behavior.

faq.question: Can it improve existing tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest stronger assertions, missing edge cases, and additional mock coverage.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
